registers.name: PsychSift answer pipeline
registers.scope: Retrieval, answer generation, citations and copy/export.
registers.authority: Static evidence register only. It does not establish clinical adequacy, regulatory classification, or risk acceptance.

hazards.title: A wrong clinical number reaches the clinician
hazards.residualRisk: Faithful-but-wrong source values and clinical plausibility remain outside deterministic numeric faithfulness proof.

hazards.title: A stale or unverified guideline is presented as current/authoritative
hazards.residualRisk: Repository controls surface review state and cap high-risk trust, but source currency and clinical validation require human authority.

hazards.title: A safety caveat present on screen is stripped on copy/export
hazards.residualRisk: Canonical answer copy preserves table and safety context; every secondary quote/export path is not asserted by one end-to-end clinical acceptance test.

hazards.title: A claim is attributed to the wrong source / a source is given false authority
hazards.residualRisk: Deterministic claim support and provenance labels do not prove that a clinically plausible source or claim is true.

hazards.title: An answer that should be withheld or flagged is presented as trusted
hazards.residualRisk: Fail-closed relevance and similarity provenance are tested, while broader confidence policy still requires clinical validation.

hazards.title: Adversarial / corrupted document content changes the answer
hazards.residualRisk: Prompt-facing identity fields are neutralized and evidence is fenced; faithful-but-wrong or corrupted clinical source content remains an open clinical-truth hazard.

openAssuranceDecisions.residualRisk: Static tests establish code behavior, not clinical truth, source authority, or clinical adequacy.
No authorised external clinical or regulatory risk acceptance is recorded.

registers.name: Caring Contacts
registers.scope: The Caring Contacts workspace only. It does not cover the answer pipeline.
registers.authority: DRAFT — requires clinical sign-off by the owner before any real-patient use. This document is a starting point assembled from what this repository already records. It is not clinical authority, it is not a risk assessment anybody has performed, and nothing in it constitutes approval of a pilot. No row below has been reviewed, accepted, or signed off by a clinician. Until the owner signs it, treat every "residual risk" cell as an unreviewed assertion by whoever drafted the row, not as an accepted level of risk.

hazards.title: No named clinical safety officer, so nobody owns clinical risk for this service
hazards.residualRisk: Requires formal human CSO appointment and signed attestation file before live mode can boot; runtime fails closed with PilotGovernanceViolationError
hazards.harm: Every hazard below is unowned. An incident has no named person to escalate to; a clinical judgement about wording, cadence or an adverse event has no author

hazards.title: The patient-visible message set has never been read by anyone with lived experience
hazards.residualRisk: The facilitation pack is ready; the physical review panel must be convened and documented before attestation sign-off
hazards.harm: A discharged patient in a suicide-aftercare programme receives wording nobody with lived experience has judged; the wording may be harmful in ways only that review would surface

hazards.title: No Aboriginal cultural safety review, in a Western Australian suicide-aftercare service
hazards.residualRisk: Formal consultation with WA Aboriginal health leadership (AHCWA/WAPHA) must be completed before live pilot
hazards.harm: Culturally unsafe contact, wording or reporting in a population where suicide aftercare carries specific and well-documented cultural safety requirements

hazards.title: Application data and SMS metadata egress outside Australia violates sovereign lock
hazards.residualRisk: Requires provisioning dedicated AWS Sydney (ap-southeast-2) or Azure Sydney (australiaeast) container environment rather than shared multi-region PaaS
hazards.harm: Identifiers, PHI, or messages process outside Australian jurisdiction, violating sovereign healthcare policy

hazards.title: Hospital referral feed feasibility is unconfirmed and is the largest programme risk
hazards.residualRisk: WA Health HSS enterprise feed onboarding timeline remains external; manual intake screen provides production fallback
hazards.harm: The service cannot start, or starts on manual entry nobody has designed for; the whole build rests on an integration nobody has confirmed is possible

hazards.title: A caring contact is delivered after the recipient has died
hazards.residualRisk: Depends entirely on the death reaching this system. Nothing here detects a death nobody reported — that is H-44's feed, unconfirmed
hazards.harm: A bereaved family receives an automated "thinking of you" message addressed to the dead person

hazards.title: A death timestamp that cannot be parsed makes the cancellation fail open
hazards.residualRisk: The exception has no defined human workflow attached to it in this repository
hazards.harm: As H-C01

hazards.title: A correction to a recorded death puts messages back in flight
hazards.residualRisk: The incident requires a human to act on it, and no on-call rota exists (H-00)
hazards.harm: Messages restart off the back of a data fix, with nobody having decided that they should

hazards.title: A third party ends a service the patient chose
hazards.residualRisk: Nothing prevents a third party from persuading the patient's own clinician to withdraw on the patient's behalf
hazards.harm: A patient loses an aftercare contact they consented to, on somebody else's say-so

hazards.title: A readmission or a changed mobile silently resumes or rebases the calendar
hazards.residualRisk: Requires a human to unpause; no reminder mechanism exists
hazards.harm: Contacts arrive on the wrong days, or resume without a human decision

hazards.title: An urgent-safety pathway retirement leaves running plans sending
hazards.residualRisk: Whether a given retirement _is_ urgent is a human judgement with no criteria written down
hazards.harm: Contacts keep going out under wording or cadence that was withdrawn for safety

hazards.title: An empty or unwritten message is sent as a caring contact
hazards.residualRisk: A sender that never calls the chokepoint meets no refusal — see the note below
hazards.harm: A person in aftercare receives a blank message, or receives nothing while the record says they were contacted

hazards.title: An implementer drafts patient-visible wording for a suicide-prevention message
hazards.residualRisk: The refusal is the whole control. The wording still has to be written, by the review H-04 names
hazards.harm: Unreviewed clinical copy reaches a discharged patient at the moment a service ends

hazards.title: A message carries commercial or risk-scoring vocabulary
hazards.residualRisk: A denylist catches known-bad words, never bad wording in general. Only the H-04 review addresses the general case
hazards.harm: A person in suicide aftercare is addressed as a marketing target or told they are "high risk"

hazards.title: A message omits how to get help
hazards.residualRisk: The required fragments are PROVISIONAL content nobody clinical has approved
hazards.harm: Someone reads a message from a mental-health service that tells them nothing about where to turn

hazards.title: A message invites a reply on a channel nobody reads
hazards.residualRisk: Only a question mark is detected. "Text back if you need us" contains none and would pass
hazards.harm: A distressed person replies expecting to be heard, and is not

hazards.title: The patient's own mobile number is echoed into the message body
hazards.residualRisk: Only checks the number the caller supplies; a stale or second number is not compared
hazards.harm: A patient receives their own number back from a service, an alarming and identifying artefact

hazards.title: A message reaches a patient carrying a number that connects to nobody
hazards.residualRisk: The acknowledgement flag exists and is greppable, but nothing stops a future caller passing it in production
hazards.harm: A person in crisis dials a number from a mental-health service and reaches dead air

hazards.title: A working crisis number is marked as fake, or the crisis sentence is reworded
hazards.residualRisk: The numbers in that sentence (Lifeline, 13YARN) are not aged by any check in this repository — see "Unverified" below
hazards.harm: The one sentence that must survive is deleted, reworded, or suppressed as synthetic

hazards.title: A message is silently split into three or more SMS segments, or truncated
hazards.residualRisk: The ceiling is only evaluated when the text is GSM-7 encodable — see H-C16
hazards.harm: A safety message arrives cut in half, or the half with the crisis number never arrives

hazards.title: A non-GSM-7 name silently disables the segment ceiling
hazards.residualRisk: The refusal is in the _name_ path only. A non-GSM-7 character introduced anywhere else in a message still bypasses the ceiling
hazards.harm: The length check at message-policy.ts:186 never runs, and nothing else is checking length

hazards.title: A contact goes out outside the approved hours
hazards.residualRisk: AWST is hard-coded. A patient outside Western Australia would receive contacts at the wrong local time
hazards.harm: An unsolicited message about suicide aftercare arrives at 3 am

hazards.title: A retry sends late rather than not at all
hazards.residualRisk: The interaction is documented and tested, but no production sender exercises it (see the B2 note)
hazards.harm: As H-C17

hazards.title: A message is dispatched against an ended, cancelled or withdrawn plan
hazards.residualRisk: Defence in depth on two layers, one of which (the chokepoint) has no production caller
hazards.harm: A withdrawn patient — or a bereaved family — receives a contact after the service ended

hazards.title: A draft or paused plan sends anyway
hazards.residualRisk: As H-C19
hazards.harm: Contacts begin before anybody activated the plan, or resume during a hold

hazards.title: A confirmed incident does not stop sending
hazards.residualRisk: Somebody has to notice and record the stop. No automatic detector exists for any of the five reasons
hazards.harm: The failure that triggered the incident keeps happening while it is being investigated

hazards.title: One person restarts a stopped service alone
hazards.residualRisk: The roles are seats nobody occupies until H-00 closes, so today one person is all there is
hazards.harm: A service stopped for a clinical or privacy incident resumes on one person's judgement

hazards.title: The incident banner leaks patient detail onto every screen
hazards.residualRisk: A future edit could widen the parameter; only the type stops it
hazards.harm: A patient's name, number or clinical note is rendered service-wide

hazards.title: An author approves their own pathway version
hazards.residualRisk: Two approvals from two people is a process control, not a competence check
hazards.harm: Clinical content ships with no independent check at all

hazards.title: One person supplies both required pathway approvals by changing role
hazards.residualRisk: As H-C22: the seats are unfilled
hazards.harm: The dual-approval record is real in form and empty in substance

hazards.title: A pathway version's approval is read as approval of the message wording
hazards.residualRisk: Depends on every screen reading the constant rather than writing its own sentence
hazards.harm: A clinician believes a discharged patient's message has been signed off when it has not

hazards.title: A clinician reads another team's patients
hazards.residualRisk: Team membership is asserted by the session, and this prototype's session model is not the eventual one
hazards.harm: Unauthorised access to identifiable mental-health records

hazards.title: Patient data leaks into the audit trail
hazards.residualRisk: A denylist of field names and one number format. A free-text field with a new name would pass unless its name is on the list
hazards.harm: The trail intended to prove good behaviour becomes a second copy of the record it audits

hazards.title: A search term or a patient's name is recorded as an audited object id
hazards.harm: The audit trail itself becomes a searchable index of what was typed about whom

hazards.title: A refused write leaves no trace
hazards.residualRisk: Only covers refusals at the boundary. A refusal further out has no record
hazards.harm: An attempted unauthorised action is invisible afterwards

hazards.title: Identifying detail is kept indefinitely
hazards.residualRisk: Seven years is a working assumption, not a legal determination — phase-1-handoff.md says so. Nothing schedules the clearance
hazards.harm: A suicide-aftercare record naming a patient persists with no end date

hazards.title: A coordinator's attestation is read as the patient's consent
hazards.residualRisk: The distinction is carried by wording and a type guard. A screen that paraphrases it loses it
hazards.harm: The service believes it holds consent it does not hold; the actual agreement lives in the hospital record

hazards.title: Training data mixes with live data
hazards.residualRisk: It is a predicate future code is _expected_ to consult; nothing forces a new query to ask
hazards.harm: Synthetic contacts are treated as real, or a real patient's data appears in a training sandbox

hazards.title: A published figure re-identifies an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander patient
hazards.residualRisk: The owner recorded on 2026-08-26 that one commit can move both the number and its pin, and accepted that gap for a prototype holding no real data. That acceptance does not survive a real-patient pilot. Connected to H-05
hazards.harm: Re-identification in a small population, in a service where that is a specific and serious harm

registers.name: Ward Flow
registers.scope: Bed matching, placement, transport and movements.
registers.authority: No hazard register has been written. Nothing here has been reviewed against one.

ledgerMentions.summary: Ward Flow: sex and gender identity are one field, and that single field drives bed matching
Ward Flow: the 'it suggests nothing' rule may be reversed, and the reversal is written down nowhere
Ward Flow: Aboriginal cultural safety review is unstarted and cannot be done by this team
Ward Flow: enforce hospital authorisation as a candidate destination constraint
Ward Flow: the Command mockup and the shipped reducer give opposite answers on a prior decline
